summary: Coordinated header override at edge bypasses tenant route pin and triggers fallback to compatibility variant
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports that during a scheduled canary of redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2, a subset (~12%) of requests from a VIP tenant were unexpectedly routed to the compatibility variant (redwood/gpt-rl-3b-compat) despite an explicit per-tenant model pin. The diversion coincided with a brief configuration change at the edge performed by BrightDocs' CDN vendor to add an 'X-Forwarded-Model' header for debugging. Impact: Inconsistent outputs for end-users, degraded quality for some sessions, and a short billing uplift for the compatibility variant.

Environment: Production (us-east-1) on Dedicated cluster assigned to BrightDocs (enterprise). Canary weight set to 10% with tenant-level pin to v2. Observed window: 2026-03-09T21:17:00Z — 2026-03-09T21:25:30Z.

Expected behavior: Tenant pin should be authoritative and prevent routing to the compat variant during canary. Actual behavior: Requests bearing X-Forwarded-Model header were preferentially assigned to compat variant, bypassing pin enforcement for a small cohort of edge-generated requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a route with tenant-level pin to redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2 and set canary weight 10%.
2) From a client simulating the BrightDocs tenant, send streams with keepalive and session tokens while adding header 'X-Forwarded-Model: gpt-rl-3b-compat'.
3) Monitor routing decisions in the orchestrator logs and edge request logs for that tenant key.
4) Observe that requests with the header are assigned to compat variant despite the pin.
logs: 2026-03-09T21:17:03Z ingress-edge-123 INFO received request tenant=brightdocs session=abcd123 headers='Host: api.redwood.ai; X-Forwarded-Model: gpt-rl-3b-compat; Cookie: tenant=brightdocs'
2026-03-09T21:17:03Z orchestrator-12 DEBUG resolve_route tenant=brightdocs pin=redwood/gpt-rl-3b-v2 edge_header_model=gpt-rl-3b-compat chosen_variant=redwood/gpt-rl-3b-compat reason='header_override'
2026-03-09T21:17:04Z serving-34 WARN fallback chosen=compat variant latency_improvement=12ms
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support confirmed customer-performed header insertion via CDN debugging change. Edge logs show header present for affected sessions. Orchestrator logs show a code path labeled 'header_override' used during routing decision.
Hypothesis A: Edge header is being treated as higher precedence than tenant pin during route resolution due to a legacy precedence table introduced in pre-2025 orchestrator refactor.
Hypothesis B: A short-lived feature flag (allow_edge_model_hint=true) was enabled in the affected edge shard for observability and wasn't gated by tenant pin checks.
Telemetry snapshot: 1.2k requests from tenant in window, ~140 (11.6%) were diverted to compat; those requests all carried X-Forwarded-Model. No other tenants exhibited the issue.
Reproducibility: Internal replay with same header reproduces diversion on staging with current orchestrator canary build. Removing header prevents diversion (pin respected).

Related code paths: router/handler.go lines with 'modelHint' precedence and orchestrator/routing_policy.go where pin enforcement should short-circuit header hints. PR candidate: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2384 addresses precedence check order.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 — Maya Thompson (Support): Notified customer and requested CDN rollback; customer confirmed they applied header injection for tracing and rolled it back at 21:27Z.
2026-03-10 10:03 — Liam O'Connor (SRE): Reproduced locally; confirmed header wins if 'allow_edge_model_hint' flag true. Marking as P1 due to enterprise customer impact.
2026-03-11 14:40 — Eng (Alejandra Ruiz): Created PR to change precedence so tenant_pin short-circuits any edge hints. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2384
2026-03-11 16:05 — Customer (BrightDocs, Hana Lee): Confirmed they removed header injection and that end-user experience normalized; asked about long-term guardrails.

2026-03-12 08:21 — Liam O'Connor: Deployed hotfix to staging and scheduled rollout to prod after canary verification. Added route-level strict_pin option to serve as immediate customer-level mitigation.
resolution: Workaround applied: Instructed BrightDocs to disable the CDN header injection (immediate). Support enabled per-tenant 'strict_pin' toggle for BrightDocs which forces pin enforcement regardless of incoming hints. Engineering fixed precedence bug in orchestrator where edge model hints could override tenant pin; patch merged (PR #2384) and hotfixed to prod during small maintenance window on 2026-03-12 02:00Z. Post-deploy telemetry shows zero further diversions for tenant. Billing uplift reconciled: credits issued for compat variant usage during incident window.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add unit/integration tests to ensure tenant pin short-circuits any edge-level model_hint (owner: orchestrator team; due: 2026-03-20).
2) Add detection rule to console to alert if >0.5% of requests for a pinned tenant are served by non-pinned variants (owner: observability; due: 2026-03-18).

3) Update runbook and customer-facing docs to call out that edge-inserted 'X-Forwarded-Model' may be treated as a hint and that strict_pin exists for enterprise tenants (owner: Support/Docs; due: 2026-03-22).
4) Audit feature flags that expose allow_edge_model_hint and ensure default is false in prod (owner: FeatureFlags; due: 2026-03-15).
5) Send post-incident summary to #support and to BrightDocs CSM (owner: Maya Thompson; due: 2026-03-13).
